Subject: Deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up

Alex — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap + next steps from our call so we all have the same context.

Call recap:
- Primary goal: embed LLM-powered summarization + search assistance into AcmeAI support flows (high-sensitivity customer data).
- Scale targets: initial steady-state QPS ~30-50 inference requests/sec, peak ~120 QPS during spikes.
- Typical input length: ~400-700 tokens (avg ~512).
- Latency target: P95 < 200ms for UI interactions; P99 (<500ms) desirable for degraded paths.
- Data requirements: data residency in US, strict access controls, audit logs, retention 1 year; SOC 2 required.

Key qualification: deployment mode
- You mentioned preference for a private VPC/on-prem evaluation because of data sensitivity, but also interest in a Hosted API for PoC to move quickly.
- Procurement is leaning toward a Reserved/Dedicated contract for production if the cost profile is acceptable.

As requested, attached is a 1-pager on deployment modes and a mutual action (MA) plan template to help capture technical + procurement milestones (Redwood_deployment_modes_one-pager.pdf, MA_plan_template.xlsx).

Immediate asks for cost modeling: could you confirm the following so we can run a tailored estimate (I can run a preliminary model and then Marissa will follow up with Dedicated capacity numbers):
1) Expected monthly active users or monthly inference requests (tokens/month if you have it).
2) % of requests that need full-context (longer seq) vs short responses (to estimate compute).
3) Any strict retention or network egress constraints beyond US residency.
4) Procurement timeline and preferred contract start date.

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up on Friday Nov 20 to review a draft cost model and deployment recommendation. Marissa (cc'd) will join to cover Dedicated capacity sizing.

Thanks — I’ll draft the initial cost model once I have the numbers below.

4AC Aditya Rao

Thanks for the recap, Aditya — this is perfect. Quick answers below to help your cost model:  

1) Monthly baseline: ~6M inference requests/month today; expected to grow to ~25-30M over 6-12 months as we expand to EU and new products.
   - Tokens: rough estimate ~12-15B tokens/month baseline (avg request ~200 tokens output + 300 tokens input).
2) Full-context requests (longer seq ~512+) are ~35% of traffic, short requests (under 256 tokens) ~65%.
3) Data residency: must be US-only for now; looking at eventual EU-onboarding in H2. Retention: 1 year for logs, raw transcripts archived offline. SOC 2 is a hard requirement.
4) Procurement timeline: initial PO expected early Jan 2027; pilot/PoC ideally in Dec 2026.

On deployment preference: for production we are leaning Dedicated (reserved capacity) if the committed cost works; would like Hosted for a fast PoC to validate UX. Private VPC is on the table if Dedicated doesn't satisfy our security team.

Can you provide a rough hosted per-token price for prototyping vs a reserved commit estimate for Dedicated (monthly cost for equivalent throughput)? Also, attach any SOC 2 / security pack or compliance overview so our security folks can pre-read.

4CB Alex Johnson
Head of Product | AcmeAI

Alex — thanks for the quick details. I put together a high-level cost model and recommendations (attached: AcmeAI_cost_model_v1.xlsx) and a short pricing summary below. This is a preliminary pass — Marissa will follow with Dedicated sizing and reserved-commit numbers during the Friday call.

Summary (high-level):
- Hosted API (best for PoC / early iteration):
  - Per-token pricing (example ballpark): $0.0008 / output-token equivalent (this is a ballpark and varies by model family).
  - Pros: no infra commit, instant rollout, Redwood-managed security options (TLS, KMS integrations).
  - Cons: higher unit cost at scale; per-token becomes expensive at 10s of millions of requests/month.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity) (best for predictable production cost):
  - Economics: reserved monthly commit -> lower $/token-equivalent as you amortize GPU pool. For your scale (~12-15B tokens/mo), reserved commit pricing typically reduces unit cost by ~40-60% vs hosted per-token pricing depending on GPU class and concurrency requirements.
  - Example ask: if you commit to a monthly throughput equivalent (we’ll translate to GPUs + slots) we can provide an exact monthly rate and burst/overage terms.
  - Pros: predictable cost, customizable SLOs, dedicated pool for lower tail latency.
  - Cons: commit required; some up-front procurement work.

- Private VPC / On-prem (best for most restrictive security requirements):
  - Economics: higher baseline (license/infra + integration/support). Typically a 1.5-2x premium vs Dedicated for the first 12 months (engineering & onboarding), but operational costs can be comparable long-term depending on your infra.
  - Pros: maximal control, fits strict security/regulatory constraints.

Recommended next steps for Friday call:
1) Marissa will present Dedicated sizing and a draft reserved-commit price sheet (we’ll bring concrete GPU counts and monthly rates).
2) We’ll review the attached cost model and I’ll walk through sensitivity scenarios (hosted vs reserved vs private).
3) If AcmeAI wants a PoC on Hosted, we can agree on a 30-60 day trial with usage caps so you can validate UX without commit.

Security pack: attaching our SOC 2 overview + compliance pack in the follow-up (Marissa/Neha will share).

Proposed time: Friday Nov 20, 10:00-10:30 PT - does that still work for you?

Thanks — putting Marissa on the follow-up to cover Dedicated details.
